title.narrative: Provision of protection and assistance to vulnerable conflict-affected people affected areas of Sudan

description.narrative: The project builds on UNHCR’s pre-existing protection interventions, structures, and facilities which support famine affected individuals in Darfur and Kordofan States. Core activities like protection monitoring will be implemented to better understand the ways in which protection incidents contribute to food insecurity and to identify and advocate for sustainable solutions. Community-based protection networks (CBPNs) will be strengthened so that they can provide broader and deeper outreach into affected communities and ensure that those most in need of timely responses are identified and referred. The multipurpose cash assistance will allow the vulnerable conflict-affected people in famine affected areas address their most pressing needs depending upon their family requirements.Protection monitoring is integral to conducting credible, evidence-based advocacy on critical protection issues faced by conflict affected people such as violations of humanitarian and human right laws amongst others. Protection monitoring is also essential to identify people with specific needs and others most in need so they can receive targeted assistance from UNHCR or be referred to specialized providers. It is also an avenue to enable communication with communities and accountability to affected population between UNHCR, its partners and conflict-affected people.In hard-to-reach areas, communities are most often the first responders and are integral to passing information and messages on the protection situation to humanitarian organizations. Therefore, CBPNs need to be established and strengthened with technical and material support to function effectively under the difficult circumstances that they face. Assistance can include training on methods of safe response and referral pathways, psychosocial first response, material support for communications, and awareness raising materials.UNHCR post distribution monitoring for cash assistance has shown that 80% of cash recipients preferred this modality of receiving humanitarian assistance. UNHCR will expand its cash assistance for basic needs into hard-to-reach and protection hotspot areas enabling conflict-affected and those at-risk of famine to better access markets to meet their urgent needs. UNHCR will partner with local and international partners and financial service providers (FSPs) to disburse funds either as cash-in-hand or digital money, whichever is most feasible. Recipients will be identified by partners, and eligibility will be verified prior to UNHCR’s approval of the distribution through the FSPs. UNHCR and/or partners will monitor the distribution and conduct spot checks for digital disbursement
